races.name: Edinburgh Childrens Hospital Charity Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mr Withington
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who rarely appears in the first half of these races; trainer Ewan Whillans has a solid 14-day strike rate and the five-year-old has form on Good, but simulated-going figures (0 wins, 0 places) on this surface and a poor recent string of 3-6-8 suggest he lacks the finishing kick to get involved from off the pace here.

runners_data.name: Gemini Man
runners_data.note: The race's key figure — Iain Jardine's eight-year-old has won twice recently including at this distance, and Kevin Stott knows his way round Musselburgh; raced six days ago which warrants monitoring, but his front-running profile is perfectly tailored to this scenario and a STYLE_FIT flag simply reflects that others cannot push him back.

runners_data.name: Jedhi Knight
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's four-year-old has placed three times over 1m4f-2m on varying ground, wears a hood, and arrives 24 days fresh; Good-ground form is modest (3 places, no wins in 15 comparable runs) and he tends to travel in midfield rather than threatening prominently, so he needs a true test to land a blow.

runners_data.name: Sophiesticate
runners_data.note: R Mike Smith's seven-year-old has been remarkably consistent — three thirds in a row on Good ground at 1m2f — and Shay Farmer's 5lb claim makes the weight attractive; she holds up naturally but her near-miss profile and high simulated-going ratio (9/15) suggest she handles the surface well, and she is the most credible threat to Gemini Man if she can sit close enough.

runners_data.name: Storm On Jura
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up fader whose recent form includes a string of mid-field finishes; Lauren Young's claim is a positive but the horse fades in the finish according to profiling and, placed into midfield by redistribution rather than natural inclination, its STYLE_FIT penalty of 0.90 reflects a real reduction in likely effectiveness here.

runners_data.name: Ivynator
runners_data.note: Jean McGregor's eight-year-old has been out 35 days and the yard has no 14-day runners to assess current form; a true hold-up type whose simulated-going record (13/15, 0W1P) is the worst in the field, and with the redistribution forcing it into an unnatural midfield spot, there is little evidence to support a bold show.

runners_data.name: Yakhabar
runners_data.note: Liam Bailey's seven-year-old ran just 14 days ago and has a placing at 1m2f on Good recently (3rd); wears a hood, and among the redistributed runners he has the most credible finishing form — three places in comparable conditions — though his natural late-running style is compromised by being pushed forward in a crowded hold-up field.

runners_data.name: Falaise Blanc
runners_data.note: Greg Fairley's four-year-old is the most consistent runner in the race by recent form — four seconds in five starts — and has strong Good-ground placed figures (6/15, 4 places); wears a visor and its natural style places it among hold-up horses, but its consistency means it is equipped to cope if funnelled into a midfield tracking role.

runners_data.name: Liberty Looming
runners_data.note: Adam Nicol's five-year-old has been off 81 days, which is the longest absence in the field and a significant fitness concern; its Good-ground record over 1m4f+ is entirely unplaced (0W0P) and the redistribution from hold-up to midfield does nothing to paper over those doubts — needs to show it retains ability after the break.

runners_data.name: Star Of Markinch
runners_data.note: A decade-old veteran who has run four consecutive fourths over 1m4-2m on Good, showing remarkable consistency without ever winning; Gary Rutherford's runner has been off 56 days and, while the distance is familiar, its STYLE_FIT penalty and redistribution from rear to midfield reflect that it is unlikely to be worse than it looks — but also unlikely to break the placed-without-winning pattern.

races.paceDynamic: Gemini Man is the lone confirmed front runner in this 1m5f handicap and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, Kevin Stott can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on Good ground at Musselburgh. The remainder of the field — Mr Withington, Jedhi Knight, Sophiesticate, Storm On Jura, Ivynator, Yakhabar, Falaise Blanc, Liberty Looming and Star Of Markinch — are all hold-up or prominent types, meaning there is no natural pressure horse to force Gemini Man off his own rhythm. This field contains far more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Storm On Jura, Ivynator, Yakhabar, Falaise Blanc, Liberty Looming and Star Of Markinch are all genuine hold-up horses but several will be shuffled forward into midfield by circumstance, with Falaise Blanc — a consistent placer — and Yakhabar most likely to secure a workable midfield berth given their recent form. A solo, uncontested lead at a fair pace on a sound surface over this trip is the single most favourable scenario for a front runner with Gemini Man's profile; the race shape strongly favours horses who can track or sit just off the pace in second or third and challenge at the two-furlong marker, since true closers launching from the rear will face a wall of traffic and a moderate overall tempo that may not suit a late, deep-seated finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gemini Man Unchallenged Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Gemini Man is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a controlled pace that does not empty the tank.
scenarios.body: Stott can manage every fraction on the Good ground and is still travelling within himself entering the straight, making it very difficult for hold-up horses to reel him in from a cold start; at OR 53 and with two recent wins at this level, his form profile fits perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Overhauled
scenarios.trigger: If a horse travelling prominently just off Gemini Man's shoulder builds a sustained challenge from the three-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Gemini Man has set things up comfortably but a rival in second or third — conserving energy behind a slow-ish pace — has enough left to run him down late; Sophiesticate's consistent recent form and Good-ground figures make her the natural beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to set up a sprint finish and the hold-up horses find clear runs through midfield traffic.
scenarios.body: Storm On Jura, Ivynator and Yakhabar would need their natural rear-running positions but are redistributed forward into midfield, undermining the credibility of this shape; should chaos in the straight create gaps, Yakhabar — who has placed at this trip on Good ground — is best placed among the back markers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Compresses Field
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is so steady that the entire field converges in a bunched finish inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A tight, muddling finish helps the horse with the clearest run and strongest finishing kick regardless of starting position; Falaise Blanc's repeated placed efforts and Jedhi Knight's placings on Good ground give them an outside chance in a messy conclusion, but this scenario depends on Gemini Man capitulating — unlikely given his recent wins.

watchPoints.text: Gemini Man's recovery time after running just six days ago warrants monitoring at the start — if he jumps sluggishly or is crowded early, the entire pace dynamic collapses and Storm On Jura and Yakhabar could benefit from the resulting scramble.

Falaise Blanc has finished second four times in recent starts and is the most likely horse to mount a sustained late challenge; watch whether Greg Fairley can find a clear run through midfield traffic in the straight, as a blocked passage would be the only thing to stop her running into a place again.

With nine of ten runners naturally inclined to hold up or race prominently off the pace, the midfield in the early stages could be unusually compressed — any stumble or interference between the start and the two-mile chute may affect Jedhi Knight and Sophiesticate, who need a clean passage to maximise their chances.

Liberty Looming's 81-day absence is the most notable fitness query in the race; if Ben Robinson pushes forward early to keep it warm, that could marginally increase the early pace and put slight pressure on Gemini Man's intended solo lead.

races.name: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Bernard Hunter Mobile Cranes Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Bigalo
runners_data.note: Held-up type with four runs on good ground and a recent second at seven furlongs at Musselburgh showing course-and-distance form; Kevin Stott is a shrewd hand here and the step up to seven suits, though no win yet from four tries
runners_data.comment: Bigalo shaped with promise when second last time out, and has run over today's trip and going — his profile makes him a strong each-way threat from stall 2, with our rating of 71 underlining his claims; the concern is that he's been winless in his last four starts.

runners_data.name: Boutblummintime
runners_data.note: 43 days off the track is the key query for Oisin McSweeney and Adrian Keatley's two-year-old; two placed efforts at six furlongs on good going show ability, but the step to seven and the layoff leave questions, and the horse's natural style won't be served if pace is absent
runners_data.comment: Boutblummintime arrives here 43 days fresh, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating puts him comfortably clear of his six rivals. Fourth last time out, he's winless in recent starts but the figures suggest he's overdue to make his mark from stall 5 off 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Aurora Valkyrie
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners a filly with a placed effort at seven furlongs on good ground in her latest run; Connor Beasley's riding style suits patient delivery, and Katie Scott has a 1/8 strike rate over 14 days, though the horse's tendency to race with cover will be tested if this becomes a dawdle-and-sprint
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, with a fifth two starts back and a lowly eighth three starts back making her hard to fancy, Aurora Valkyrie does at least return after 25 days with distance and going experience to call on, though she faces a stiff task from stall 6 on a mark of 61.

runners_data.name: Liveadream
runners_data.note: Phillip Makin's runner showed a clear step forward when finishing second at seven furlongs on good ground recently and arrives fresh on a seven-day turnaround; despite being a natural hold-up type, the horse's placed run at this trip suggests it can find a position closer to the pace when the race demands it, which is a live angle here
runners_data.comment: Liveadream shaped with promise when second two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, so conditions hold no fears; at 131 lb and yet to win in her last four starts, she'll need to find more than that placed effort suggests.

runners_data.name: Tiger In The Tree
runners_data.note: Consistent place-getter at seven and eight furlongs on good ground with five qualifying runs in similar conditions — the experience stands out in this nursery field; Tim Easterby's yard is firing (7/91 over 14 days) and headgear (p) could sharpen the response, though the horse is also being asked to race in a shape that doesn't suit a pure hold-up
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five, Tiger In The Tree does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and back-to-back thirds give her a platform; a rating of 62 suggests more ability than her official mark of 51 implies, though stepping up from that level remains the test.

runners_data.name: Amantha
runners_data.note: The only winner in the field having scored at seven furlongs on good ground, and Ben Robinson's booking suggests connections are bullish; Brian Ellison's 0/26 14-day strike rate is a concern, but the form line reads well for this trip and going, and Amantha is the likeliest candidate to press forward if the pace is pedestrian
runners_data.comment: Amantha shaped well last time out, finishing second, and followed up a win two starts back — she has experience over today's trip and going, and stall one could prove interesting. The concern is her trainer's current run of 0 from 26 over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Bluestone Lady
runners_data.note: Headgear (b) worn and a placed effort at seven furlongs recently, but Phillip Makin has 0/2 over 14 days and the horse's four-run sequence without a win raises questions; the blinkers are a potential wildcard if they sharpen focus, though Bluestone Lady would need to overcome a tendency to race with the field from the rear
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Bluestone Lady nevertheless showed ability with a second two runs back, and she has run over today's distance and going before; ranked sixth of seven on our figures, however, she faces a stiff task from stall seven carrying 132 lb.

races.paceDynamic: With every single runner in this seven-horse field carrying a hold-up profile, there is no confirmed front-runner to set a conventional pace, meaning the field will likely crawl away from the gates before compressing into a sprint finish over the final two furlongs. The absence of any genuine pace-setter creates a vacuum at the front that could be exploited by whoever is most willing to press forward from the off, potentially rewarding the boldest jockey rather than the most naturally front-running horse. Amantha, with a recent win on the board and strong good-going form, and Liveadream, who has shown ability to race prominently when conditions demand, look the most likely to drift toward the front if no natural leader emerges. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a sharp late turn of foot who can produce a sustained finishing kick in the final furlong — pure stamina-grinders will be disadvantaged by the stop-start tempo, and horses who need cover and a strong pace to run into will be left vulnerable.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls through the early stages and the race becomes a massed sprint over the final two furlongs
scenarios.body: A slow early tempo compresses the field so that positions matter little until the furlong pole, at which point acceleration and a clear passage are everything; horses with a sharp, short finishing kick over seven furlongs on good ground are best placed to capitalise

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Bold Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If one jockey takes matters into their own hands and sends their mount to the front to control from halfway
scenarios.body: With no natural pace-setter, a runner willing to stride on from halfway could set a manageable gallop and dictate to the field, denying closers the strong pace they need; Amantha's recent winning form and Liveadream's placed run at seven furlongs make both plausible candidates to fill this role

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If a moderate pace is set and runners with genuine late-race acceleration can thread through in the final furlong
scenarios.body: A sustained but not extreme gallop would give the horses settled toward the rear time to find their stride and deliver a run, though the caveat is that most hold-up types here are operating somewhat out of their natural role given the race shape; Bigalo's recent second at seven furlongs on good ground and Boutblummintime's consistent form make them the most credible beneficiaries

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Pair Draw Clear
scenarios.trigger: If two horses break more alertly than the rest and establish a meaningful lead through the first three furlongs
scenarios.body: A small breakaway group setting a genuine pace would string out the field and suit runners with both tactical speed and stamina to see out a strong seven furlongs; Tiger In The Tree's repeated placed finishes at seven furlongs on good ground give it a slender claims here

watchPoints.text: Amantha is the only winner in the field and if Ben Robinson elects to press forward given the absent pace, it could easily control this race and prove very difficult to peg back
With seven hold-up types and no natural front-runner, the early stages may be almost stationary — watch for a chaotic mid-race scramble for position as jockeys suddenly realise no one is leading
Liveadream arrives on a seven-day turnaround, which can signal a confident yard sending a fresh horse in good form, making it one to monitor in the market before post time

Tiger In The Tree wearing headgear (p) for the first time or recently — Tim Easterby's volume operation (7/91 over 14 days) means these runners can land at a price when the yard is in form and equipment changes are deployed

races.name: Bernard Hunter Metal Recycling Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Jer Batt
runners_data.note: Front-runner holding a clear tactical advantage as the lone pace-setter; David & Nicola Barron yard is 1/6 in the last 14 days but Jer Batt returns after a 96-day absence with no recent sharpness, and its six similar-going runs show zero wins and only four places — fitness is the key concern.|
runners_data.comment: Jer Batt has been placed three times in his last five starts, most recently third, and has run over today's trip and going, giving him a solid profile as the top-rated runner here; 96 days off is a watch, but at 136 lb from stall four he retains clear claims.

runners_data.name: Mighty Magnus
runners_data.note: The three-year-old holds the strongest similar-going record in the field with two wins and six places from thirteen Good-ground runs, and Michael Dods is 6/27 in form; a natural hold-up runner who needs the pace to be honest to deliver his finish, and a 27-day break looks fine.|
runners_data.comment: Mighty Magnus arrives fresh on 27 days' rest with distance and going experience in his favour, and that win three starts back underlines his ability to deliver on the day; the concern is he has been held to third or worse in his two most recent outings.

runners_data.name: Francisco's Piece
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's runner has no wins or placings from seven attempts on Good going and the recent form string of 0-0-5-7-5 gives little confidence; a hold-up style that requires a truly contested gallop leaves this horse dependent on others for everything.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Francisco's Piece nevertheless carries an 85 rating into this and has run over today's trip and going — the back-to-back fifths either side of a seventh two starts back suggest consistency of a kind, though converting that into a finish is the obvious concern after 52 days off.

runners_data.name: Montezuma
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old has placed three times from eight Good-ground runs and has back-to-back runner-up finishes at five furlongs on Good and Soft; wears a hood, returns after 44 days, and with Lauren Young's 5lb claim keeping the weight manageable, tracking Jer Batt from a prominent pitch is the ideal map position.|
runners_data.comment: Montezuma shaped well when third last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, making him a genuine threat from stall two on 132 lb; the main concern is that he has found one or more rivals too strong in recent starts, and our rating suggests he may be marginally exposed in this company.

runners_data.name: Curious Rover
runners_data.note: Won over this exact course and distance on Good ground 18 days ago and is the freshest horse in the race; a genuine hold-up type placed on the midfield map purely because multiple closers cannot all sit at the back — Kevin Stott will need to find room late, and the tight five-runner field may actually aid that rather than hinder it.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of five on our figures, and his record of one win in his last six starts — albeit that success came last time out — makes him hard to fancy at the weights carrying 130 lb; has run over today's trip and going, which at least is something.

races.paceDynamic: Jer Batt is the lone confirmed front-runner in this five-runner 5f handicap at Musselburgh, and with only Montezuma offering any prominent-style company, the pace is unlikely to be pressured or contested hard — Jer Batt should settle into a comfortable lead and control tempo throughout. Montezuma will attempt to sit close behind but with a hold-up contingent of Mighty Magnus, Francisco's Piece, and Curious Rover all tracking from off the pace, the mid-to-rear portion of the field will be compact and reliant on the front end not collapsing. Curious Rover is a genuine hold-up horse redistributed to midfield on the map purely because this field contains more natural hold-up types than the diagram can accommodate at the rear — in reality Curious Rover, Mighty Magnus, and Francisco's Piece are all true come-from-behind runners chasing the same ground late. The race shape strongly favours a prominent or front-running profile: a single uncontested pace-setter dictating from the front on Good ground over five furlongs at a track that does not overly bias one style is a classic setup for the leader to dictate and the closers to need a genuine late burst — horses racing close to the pace with tactical cover will be best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Jer Batt leads uncontested and sets a fair but not suicidal gallop on Good ground.
scenarios.body: Jer Batt dictates every yard and with no rival willing to match strides, the pace is measured enough to deny the closers a true target to run at. Montezuma, tracking in second, is best placed of all to pounce if the leader tires in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Jer Batt sets enough of a clip to tire late and Montezuma times a challenge to perfection from second.
scenarios.body: Montezuma has form figures of 2-1 at five furlongs on Good going and Lauren Young's 5lb claim helps offset the weight; sitting a length off the leader throughout, a smooth challenge inside the final furlong suits this profile ideally. Jer Batt may still be involved but Montezuma's recent course-and-distance record makes this the most credible alternative shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If Jer Batt and Montezuma burn enough fuel setting a strong tempo that the hold-up horses catch them flat-footed.
scenarios.body: Mighty Magnus has two wins from ten starts on Good going over this trip and Connor Beasley will be alive to any injection of pace that creates a gap to exploit late; Curious Rover's recent win came on Good ground and a fast-run race is exactly the shape that brings its finishing kick into play. The redistribution of both hold-up runners to midfield on the map is a mapping artefact — they are true come-from-behind types and need a strong gallop, which is not guaranteed here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Affair, Rank Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses, the field bunches and Francisco's Piece finds a clear run from a clear passage out wide.
scenarios.body: Francisco's Piece has struggled for form with a recent string of zeros and has no wins or places on Good ground from 15 attempts, making this a low-probability scenario reliant on something going wrong elsewhere. Even in a messy race its form profile offers little encouragement, and this scenario is included only because any five-runner scramble can occasionally produce a surprising result.

watchPoints.text: Jer Batt's 96-day absence means fitness is unproven — watch the market closely; if it drifts significantly it may not be fully wound up and the race shape advantage narrows.|

Curious Rover's true running style is hold-up despite its midfield map position — Stott will drop it in and hunt for a gap, so watch for crowding on the rail in the final furlong with multiple closers hunting the same space.|

Montezuma wears a hood and is the most likely horse to challenge Jer Batt for the lead early — if Lauren Young pushes up to sit upsides rather than just off the pace, the race tempo could increase sharply and change the shape entirely.|
Francisco's Piece has a dismal record on Good going and is likely to be significant in the market as an indicator of value elsewhere — its odds will tell you more about the race than its form.|

races.name: East Air Conditioning Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Braes Of Doune
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner in the race with course and trip form in similar going (2 wins, 7 places from 15 Good-ground starts); Jim Goldie in decent 14-day form at 3/46, Lauren Young 5lb claim adds value, the solo lead is an enormous tactical gift at this track even if her OR of 55 is modest.
runners_data.comment: Braes Of Doune holds the highest rating in this field and has run over today's trip and going, while 18 days gives him a fresh but race-fit look from stall three; the concern is he's winless in his last five starts, with a pair of sixths most recently.

runners_data.name: King Sharja
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up operator with two seconds at this exact 7f distance in Good-to-firm/Good conditions for Ruth Carr; best deployed from the rear but risks being left with too much to do if Braes Of Doune doesn't stretch the field, moderate sim-going strike rate of 9/15.
runners_data.comment: Consecutive seconds two and three starts back show King Sharja has the class to threaten here, and his experience over today's trip and going is a clear asset at 135 lb from stall six; yet to land it in recent starts, and that unplaced effort last time is the note of caution.

runners_data.name: Monhammer
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old true hold-up horse who has placed in four of last five 7f starts on Good ground, but is naturally rear-dwelling and has been mapped forward only because the field is saturated with closers; Harry Burns's 3lb claim helps, though Linda Perratt's 14-day record of 4/13 is notable positively.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Monhammer does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a second three starts back shows he can threaten — but a sixth last time out and our rating sitting above his official mark of 48 suggest he faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Misemerald
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer in five-year-old form with three recent places at 7f-8f on Good, wearing headgear and returning after just 15 days; Philip Kirby's yard at 0/13 in the 14-day window is a negative trainer flag, and she is a true closer who will need a stronger pace than this race looks likely to produce.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked last on our figures, Misemerald is hard to fancy despite some consistency — third and second in recent starts suggest she finds a way to be competitive, and she has run over today's trip and going before from stall one carrying 126 lb.

runners_data.name: Wait For It
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who shaped best over shorter trips and on Good ground (two places from three runs on that surface) but her 8f and Tapeta form is weak; Liam Bailey at 0/10 in 14-day window is concerning, and as one of the truest hold-up horses in the race she is most vulnerable in a slow-tempo, front-runner scenario.
runners_data.comment: Placed in each of her last two starts, Wait For It arrives here just nine days on from her most recent effort in fine heart. She has run over today's trip and going before, and a speed rating of 61 suggests she has more ability than her official mark of 45 implies, though she remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: April Diamond
runners_data.note: Struggled on sprint distances recently (13th at 6f, mostly 5f-6f form) and drops back from shorter trips, so the step up to 7f is a query; sim-going record at 3/5 is small sample, and as a hold-up horse drawn into a field that doesn't suit closers, her recent 0-placing run (form: 76520) is not encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts with only a single runner-up finish to show, April Diamond is hard to fancy stepping back in after an unplaced effort 25 days ago; she has run over today's trip and going, and stall two is her lot at 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Sanditon
runners_data.note: Has a win and multiple places at 7f and is returning on 17 days in headgear for Charlie Johnston (3/45 in 14-day window); though a natural hold-up type, his recent runs suggest he is capable of pushing forward early, making him one of the most likely to actually secure a prominent berth rather than being stranded at the rear.
runners_data.comment: Sanditon showed his best when winning four starts back, and he arrives here on a handy 17-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and conditions. The concern is his inconsistency, with fifth last time out following a seventh two starts back.

races.paceDynamic: Braes Of Doune is the lone confirmed front-runner in this seven-furlong handicap and, with no genuine pressurer to push against, is set to dictate an honest but sustainable gallop from the gates on Good ground at Musselburgh. The remainder of the field is stacked with hold-up horses — Sanditon, Monhammer, Misemerald, Wait For It, King Sharja, and April Diamond all want to race off the pace — meaning Braes Of Doune can control tempo entirely on her own terms without any rival willing to take her on. This overwhelmingly favours a front-runner-leads, prominent-racer-wins shape: a solo, uncontested lead at a manageable pace rewards those who can sit just off the pace and kick, not those buried deep in a hold-up position chasing a gallop that was never fast enough to set them up. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than can realistically get their preferred rear position; Sanditon and Monhammer, the two with the best recent form at this track and trip, are most likely to push forward into a prominent berth closer to Braes Of Doune, while King Sharja and Wait For It will be the truest hold-up operators from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Braes Of Doune Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Braes Of Doune leads without any sustained pressure and sets a fair-to-slow pace that suits hold-up horses positioned prominently.
scenarios.body: Braes Of Doune controls every yard and the race becomes a test of who can get closest to her through the turn and quicken into the straight; runners who track within two lengths of the leader have a decisive positional advantage on this track.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Sweep Past
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is quick enough to string the field out and those who sit just off Braes Of Doune have the reserves to collar her in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Braes Of Doune sets the fractions but a prominent runner like Sanditon, having tracked efficiently, picks her off inside the final furlong as the leader's effort flattens out; this is the most likely scenario if early splits are sharper than expected.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is surprisingly strong, creates a genuine test, and the closers get a true run off a fast tempo through the dip.
scenarios.body: King Sharja or Wait For It, given a fast enough gallop to chase, deliver a finishing burst from the rear and collar the front three inside the final furlong; this scenario is structurally unlikely given the field composition and the preponderance of hold-up types all needing the same fast pace to ignite.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple hold-up horses break their style and try to push forward early, creating a contested lead and chaotic early positions.
scenarios.body: With several horses stepping out of their natural role to avoid being trapped at the back in a slow-pace race, positional jostling in the first two furlongs disrupts rhythm and leaves the race open to any horse who settles best; Braes Of Doune's advantage narrows if she is unexpectedly challenged from the off.

watchPoints.text: Braes Of Doune's ability to get away cleanly from the gates and establish the lead unchallenged is the single most important moment of this race — any stumble or slow break that lets another runner take her rail position transforms the entire race shape.

Sanditon and Monhammer are the most likely to break their natural hold-up style and push into prominent positions; watch for them in the first furlong — if both commit forward, it creates a mini-pace battle that could compromise all three of their finishes.

Wait For It and Misemerald are both true hold-up horses mapped artificially forward — if the pace is modest, they will arrive too late regardless of finishing speed, so watch for their jockeys (Garritty, Stott) attempting to slot closer than usual from the off.

King Sharja's two 2nd-place finishes over this exact course and distance on Good ground for James Sullivan make him the most proven closer in the field at this track — monitor whether Sullivan elects to push forward rather than accept a rear position in a slow-pace scenario.

April Diamond's recent form is all at 5f-6f and she has never shown she truly gets 7f — watch her behaviour in the final two furlongs to see whether the extra furlong finds her out on Good ground at Musselburgh.

races.name: Lens Self Storage Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Inappropriate
runners_data.note: Capable stayer with good-ground wins at 2m-range trips and recent placed efforts on similar going, wears tongue-pin; races from the rear and will need a strong pace to deliver her finishing effort, 18 days since last run is fine but her record shows she often runs into a place rather than wins.
runners_data.comment: Inappropriate has been knocking on the door, finishing second last time out and second four starts back, with going experience in his favour and a race-fit 18-day turnaround lending further appeal; the concern is he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Teofimo
runners_data.note: Held-up type whose recent form string shows nothing better than sixth since a break, and his historical record on good ground — six runs, no wins, two places — is modest; 40 days off adds a fitness query at 2m on turf, and trainer Adam Nicol has a quiet 14-day record of 0/2.
runners_data.comment: Teofimo posted a second three starts back on today's going, and our rating has him as the one to beat in this field — but he's winless in his last four starts and back-to-back eighths and sevenths demand respect for those shortcomings.

runners_data.name: Clansman
runners_data.note: In-form eight-year-old with back-to-back wins at Southwell recently, but those came on the all-weather and this good-turf 2m trip represents a different challenge; his natural instinct is to come from off the pace, yet the crowded hold-up group means Billy Garritty may find him racing closer than ideal, reducing the impact of his finishing kick.
runners_data.comment: Clansman landed a win two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, but a below-par effort last time tempers expectations, and he carries 131 lb off a rating of 71.

runners_data.name: Arrange
runners_data.note: Veteran who has won over 2m on good ground at this course — the most relevant positive — and David Nolan's booking is an upgrade; racing out of his natural rear position into midfield for this analysis, and a 39-day absence for an eight-year-old is worth noting, though his best Musselburgh form keeps him firmly in the mix.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and third four starts back, Arrange has shown she can hit the frame and her experience over today's trip and going is a plus; winless in her last five starts is the caveat, but at 129 lb she looks an interesting each-way proposition fresh off a 39-day break.

runners_data.name: Simple Star
runners_data.note: Two wins from 15 runs on good ground at 2m-range distances signals genuine course-and-distance competence; naturally a hold-up horse drawn into a midfield role here by the crowded rear, and Connor Beasley's familiarity with the course helps, though the STYLE_FIT of 0.93 is a mild caution if the race doesn't set up as a true stamina test.
runners_data.comment: Simple Star has run over today's trip and going, shaped with promise when second two starts back, and at 128 lb steps out on a snappy 18-day turnaround with his rating of 73 giving him a competitive edge — though he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Gallus Norman
runners_data.note: The most eye-catching recent form in the field — winner at 16f on good and 15f on soft, with consistent placed efforts — and Jake Dickson's 5lb claim is a useful weight relief; true hold-up style is compromised by redistribution to midfield, but his raw form figures over staying trips on this going make him the most natural beneficiary of a Cascade Hall-led moderate gallop.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Gallus Norman is hard to fancy despite two wins in his last five starts; he has experience of today's distance and going, and a 42-day absence at least means he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Cascade Hall
runners_data.note: Mapped to the lead as the likeliest pace-setter, though she is genuinely a hold-up horse — her 0.80 STYLE_FIT is the most significant redistribution penalty in the field; Lauren Young's 5lb claim is a practical benefit if she does bowl along, and her recent 2m win on good ground confirms she handles the trip, but racing so far out of role over this stamina test is a material risk.
runners_data.comment: Cascade Hall has placed on three of his last four starts — third last time out — and has run over today's distance and going before, so conditions aren't unknown; but ranked sixth of seven on our figures, he faces a stiff task against stronger-rated rivals here.

races.paceDynamic: Cascade Hall is the lone confirmed pace-setter in this 2m handicap at Musselburgh, mapping to the lead despite being a natural hold-up type — she is the most likely candidate to dictate from the front given the absence of any genuine front-runner in the field. With Clansman, Arrange, Simple Star, and Gallus Norman all redistibuted from their natural rear positions into midfield on the map, this field contains significantly more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate, meaning several will be forced closer to the pace than they would ideally like. The result is a race likely run at a sustainable, uncontested gallop set by Cascade Hall, with a compressed midfield group tracking behind before a stamina-test develops in the final half-mile over this 2m trip on good turf. That moderate, controlled pace favours genuine stayers who can improve through a tiring field in the straight, and horses carrying class form over this sort of distance — the tactical verdict is that hold-up types with proven 2m ability and strong finishing kicks are best placed, though those forced to race further forward than suits them face a stylistic compromise that tempers their chance.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cascade Hall Controls Serenely
scenarios.trigger: If Cascade Hall is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a measured gallop that stretches the field over the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: Cascade Hall dictates every yard at a pace that suits no finisher, and her proven ability over 2m on good ground at this course means she could simply outstay rivals who have been pulled out of their comfort zones tracking her. Horses with confirmed stamina and form at the trip — Gallus Norman and Simple Star — are best placed to run her down if she ties up late, but any momentum break works against the compressed hold-up group.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stamina Grind Suits Late Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to take the sting out of the field, setting up a proper stamina finish in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: A sustainable but honest gallop gradually stretches the field, leaving the most effective stayers to pick up the pieces from behind in the final two furlongs; Gallus Norman's recent form — two wins at 15f-16f on good and good-to-soft — makes him a natural beneficiary of this shape. Simple Star has a consistent 2m record and Connor Beasley's experience at this track adds further appeal in a scenario that plays to true staying types.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Pack Swamps Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed midfield group moves collectively and overwhelms a tiring Cascade Hall approaching the final bend.
scenarios.body: With multiple hold-up types forced to race closer than natural, if they collectively quicken from the turn they could sweep past a front-runner who has been racing out of role; Arrange's course form at 2m on good ground — and David Nolan's tactical awareness — positions him well in this shape. Clansman's recent win at Southwell over 16f signals he is in form, but his all-weather record and redistribution from his true position limits confidence over this turf trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Pair Dominate Draw
scenarios.trigger: If Cascade Hall finds an early companion and two horses simply grind out the field on a strong, relentless gallop.
scenarios.body: Two horses racing at the front on good ground over 2m would produce a searching test that punishes closers who cannot sustain a challenge over the trip; neither Teofimo nor Inappropriate has the recent profile to suggest they will power past a front-running pair, making this scenario highly punishing for the entire hold-up contingent. This is a low-probability shape because no genuine second pace-setter is evident in the data, but the condensed field makes an accidental breakaway by one of the prominent types possible.

watchPoints.text: Cascade Hall — watch whether Lauren Young elects to use her early foot or drops her in behind; if she settles off the pace as her natural style dictates, there may be no true pace-setter at all and the race could develop chaotically.

Gallus Norman — Jim Goldie has saddled Cascade Hall in the same race, so watch for any stable tactics between the two; if Cascade Hall leads and Gallus Norman tracks her in second, Goldie could have the race set up ideally for both runners.

Arrange — his one 2m win at Musselburgh on good ground is directly relevant form, and with David Nolan aboard there is jockey class here that the odds may not fully reflect; watch for him being delivered with a single smooth challenge if the pace is honest.

Teofimo — 40 days off and a form string that reads 6278/ on turf; if he shows any early signs of sluggishness or gets detached early in a slowly-run race, he becomes irrelevant and his hold-up style offers no recovery mechanism at this trip.

Simple Star and Clansman — both hold-up types forced into the midfield map position; watch whether they are comfortable tracking the pace through the first mile, as either dropping out tamely or getting into a battle to stay in touch would signal their chance has gone early.

races.name: Graham + Sibbald And Neilsons Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Thornaby Pearl
runners_data.note: The in-form leader of this race with a 2W5P record on similar Good going and two wins from her last five over this exact trip; Jake Dickson's 5lb claim reduces weight meaningfully and her previous Musselburgh form is strong — the dominant tactical asset in this field.
runners_data.comment: Thornaby Pearl arrives on the back of a win last time out and a second before that, bringing smart recent momentum into this; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, and the main risk is whether 139 lb blunts his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Thunderstorm Katie
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's filly has run into a wall of placed finishes without converting (four seconds from last five), and her 1W4P similar-going record underlines consistency without a decisive winning move; Billy Garritty rides, but a repeat placed effort looks her ceiling here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts despite three runner-up finishes, Thunderstorm Katie has struggled to convert and ranks fifth of six on our figures; she has run over today's distance and going before, and 20 days since her last outing leaves her reasonably fresh, but she remains hard to fancy at these weights.

runners_data.name: Peregrine Falcon
runners_data.note: Harry Burns claims 3lb for a Patrick Morris yard that has sent this horse exclusively to Southwell this year — five runs on the all-weather — making Musselburgh's Good turf a genuine unknown; 57 days off and no turf form in recent history demands caution despite decent placed form.
runners_data.comment: Peregrine Falcon has shown consistent placing ability, finishing third last time out and third and second in recent starts, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions — though winless in her last five, the chief concern is whether she can finally convert that placed form into something more.

runners_data.name: Golden Havana
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' three-year-old carries a visor for the first time and returns just three days after his last run, suggesting the trainer sees him ready to fire; six consecutive placed finishes at 5f on Good going make him the most reliable off-the-pace threat in this field, and Connor Beasley's booking adds confidence.
runners_data.comment: Golden Havana has been a model of consistency, placing second three times in his last six starts, and he has experience of today's distance and going — drawn in stall three carrying 135 lb, he is the one to side with, albeit still seeking that elusive first win.

runners_data.name: South Parade
runners_data.note: Recent form shows finishes of 6-9-4-7-12 at this trip, and while Richard & David Fahey's runner is a true hold-up horse by nature, the field shape pushes him forward on the map to a position that is not his own — a 9/15 similar-going placed record flatters a horse who has struggled for finishing position repeatedly.
runners_data.comment: South Parade shaped with a shade of promise when fourth three starts back, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 66 suggests she's capable of threatening here — yet winless in her last six starts and a trainer firing at just 3% lately are real negatives.

runners_data.name: Wee Mary
runners_data.note: Headgear (hood) is noted and she arrives on a short 4-day turnaround for Jim Goldie, who is in decent form at 3/46 over 14 days; by instinct a front-running or prominent type, she is unable to secure that position in this configuration, which materially weakens her tactical chances despite a 1W5P similar-going record.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts with a string of fourth-place finishes, Wee Mary heads here just four days after her latest effort and ranks last on our figures; she has run over today's trip and going before, and stall one is hers to use.

races.paceDynamic: Thornaby Pearl is the confirmed front-runner here, and with only one horse willing to go from the gates on a flat 5f at Musselburgh, she sets a sustainable, uncontested pace that hands the early fractions entirely to her own judgement. Thunderstorm Katie will press from a prominent position but is unlikely to force a true test, meaning the gallop should be honest without becoming a burn-up. The redistributed runners tell an important story: Wee Mary is a natural prominent type who cannot get to the front in this configuration, and South Parade is a genuine hold-up horse pushed forward on the map because the rear of the field is already congested — neither will race where they want to. This shape overwhelmingly favours horses who can track the leader in second or third and use the steady, unpressured pace to quicken in the final furlong, meaning prominent-to-midfield types with a strong finishing record at this trip on Good ground hold the clearest tactical edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Thornaby Pearl Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Thornaby Pearl dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and kicks clear inside the final furlong before rivals can respond.
scenarios.body: Thornaby Pearl's form reads 1-1 in her last four at 5f on Good going, and a solo lead at Musselburgh over this flat track means she sets her own terms throughout; her yard sends her here at OR 64 with a 2W5P similar-going record that backs up the danger of a fast-finishing challenge arriving too late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly more honest than expected and the true closers find a clear run in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Golden Havana and Peregrine Falcon have both posted a sequence of placed finishes at 5f on Good and have the profile to benefit if the front-runners tie each other up even marginally; Golden Havana's visor and Connor Beasley's confident booking after only a 3-day break suggests a horse freshened and ready to pounce.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Blows Up
scenarios.trigger: If Thunderstorm Katie or Wee Mary pushes forward aggressively and forces a contested gallop that burns out the leaders.
scenarios.body: An unexpected injection of speed pressure in the opening two furlongs would leave Thornaby Pearl vulnerable late, opening the door for the hold-up horses tracking behind to sprint past tiring rivals; Golden Havana, who has finished placed in six consecutive starts, is best placed to capitalise from a patient mid-race position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Wee Mary or South Parade overcome their unfavourable race shape and find a clean passage to challenge.
scenarios.body: Both horses are racing out of role — Wee Mary as a natural prominent type mapped back to midfield, South Parade as a genuine hold-up runner who can't get his usual rear position — and history of racing against your style in a 5f sprint rarely ends well on a flat track like Musselburgh; only a significant underperformance from all other principals brings either into the frame.

watchPoints.text: Thornaby Pearl's ability to control fractions entirely unchallenged is the single biggest race-shape factor — watch whether she is allowed to bowl along or whether Thunderstorm Katie or Wee Mary push up to press her before the halfway point.

Wee Mary's 4-day turnaround and hood application could see Lauren Young (5) push forward early regardless of the race shape — if she does, she turns a controlled single-pace race into a more contested sprint and changes every other runner's tactical calculation.

Peregrine Falcon's switch from Southwell all-weather to Musselburgh Good turf after 57 days off is a significant unknown — Harry Burns' 3lb claim helps the handicapper but the surface and course change warrants monitoring in the betting market for unexpected drift.

Golden Havana's visor fitting and rapid 3-day return is a trainer signal worth tracking — if Michael Dods is shortening the horse's turn-around with fresh headgear, watch whether the market shortens him further as a sign the yard expects a sharp improvement.
